A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, methods, datasets and models. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments measuring biases in four pretrained and retrained MLMs, including benchmark scores, human-annotation alignment, retraining error rates and statistical comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results in Tables 2–3 and Appendices K–Q, including pretrained bias scores, human-annotation ROC curves and retraining evaluations.

M1.justification: Iterative token masking, prediction-quality measures, attention-weighted variants and BSP/BSR aggregation remain unchanged. v1 Equations 9–16 correspond to v2 Equations 3–10; the rewritten explanation and package announcement introduce no demonstrated algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine CrowS-Pairs bias categories and four StereoSet intrasentence categories, and retrain on the same stereotypical or anti-stereotypical CrowS-Pairs sentence sets. No dataset, language, domain or distinct evaluation scenario is added.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain CSPS, SSS, AUL and AULA comparisons. Although v2's ROC captions omit CPS/CSPS, its curve remains in Figures 4–5, which reproduce the plots from v1 Figure 3; this is not comparator removal.

E3.justification: The four model configurations, casing choices, special-token exclusions, 80/20 training-validation split, 0.15 masking probability and 30 retraining epochs are retained. Human-annotation classification still uses 58 unbiased and 1,450 biased pairs, and retraining alignment still uses 72 predictions per measure.

E4.justification: The case study illustrating how retraining changes token predictions is reduced: v1 Tables 4–5 report masked 'ignorant' and 'money' examples, whereas v2 Table 1 retains only 'money'. The broader race-bias and retraining analyses remain, largely relocated to appendices.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Shapiro-Wilk normality checks, two-tailed Welch tests and McNemar tests with the same significance-reporting conventions. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or another uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Matched bias-score tables, retraining error rates, significance outcomes and ROC AUCs are unchanged. Limited results are removed: four masked-'ignorant' prediction/rank entries from v1 Tables 4–5 and the individual CRR ECDF curves in v1 Figure 2; the ECDF-difference plot survives as v2 Figure 3.

T1.justification: All sixteen displayed equations are retained through renumbering and relocation, including baseline definitions moved to Appendices B–G. The CRR bounds and bias-score definitions are unchanged, and neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1's abstract and introduction assert superior agreement with human annotations; v2 removes that headline superiority assertion and qualifies the comparison in Section 3.4.2. The central prediction-quality and retraining-bias contributions remain, while a package release is newly claimed.

C2.justification: Section 5 explicitly discusses English-only, binary sentence-pair coverage, dependence on human annotations and generalization beyond tested models and retraining conditions. Section 2.3 adds a rationale for attention as token importance. Interpretations of the retained bias and retraining results largely persist.

D1.justification: v2 newly announces a package for computing bias scores on user-supplied or benchmark datasets. However, the PDF provides no package name or access instructions, so actual availability cannot be established. Model identifiers, hardware and documented training settings are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhao et al. (2018, 2019) to motivate retraining-based validation through debiasing and counterfactual-data research, plus references for GLUE, RACE and SQuAD. Updates to WEAT, BERT, StereoSet and Transformers references concern existing works rather than new research coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten, with explicit contribution bullets and new Limitations and Ethical Considerations sections. Method background moves into Related Work, experiments and methodology are reorganized under Section 3, and equations and detailed analyses are redistributed across Appendices A–Q.

P2.justification: Numerous figures and tables move between the main text and appendices. The overall-score table is transposed and shaded, prediction tables are merged, ROC panels are split and reordered, and one ECDF panel is removed. v2 Table 2 also incorrectly defines the distilled-model abbreviation D- as 'retrained'.

improvement.justification: v2 presents clearer contributions and better-bounded conclusions through its qualified human-annotation claim and explicit Section 5 limitations, while retaining the main empirical evidence. These modest gains outweigh the limited loss of illustrative results and new caption errors, including Table 2's incorrect D- definition. The package announcement lacks access instructions and therefore does not establish a substantial reproducibility gain.
